  "interactive_layout": "# Keys Own the Cliff
### Why half of a language model's memory can be crushed for free — and the other half cannot

---

Every time a language model produces a word, it consults everything it has already read. It does not re-read it: it keeps, for each earlier token, two vectors — a **key** and a **value**. The keys are the labels on a filing cabinet; the values are the contents of the folders. A **query** is compared against every key, the comparison decides which folders matter, and the answer is a weighted blend of those folders' contents.

That filing cabinet is enormous, so it gets compressed. And here is the surprise this page is about:

> **Compressing the values to 4 bits is free. Compressing the keys to 4 bits destroys the model.** Not degrades — destroys. In a controlled measurement, the damage ratio between the two halves was about $214{,}000$ to one.

By the end of this page you will know exactly why that had to happen, and how many bits each half deserves.

---

## 1. The measurement that started it

A model is scored by **perplexity** — roughly, how surprised it is by text it has not seen. A healthy score on this text slice is $7.11$. Now compress the cache four ways:

| what was compressed to 4 bits | perplexity | change |
|---|---|---|
| keys **and** values, scale-and-offset format | $3{,}158.07$ | $+44{,}322\%$ |
| keys **and** values, nonuniform codebook | $1{,}627.35$ | $+22{,}790\%$ |
| **keys only** | $2{,}537.80$ | $+35{,}597\%$ |
| **values only** | $7.1211$ | $+0.166\%$ |

Two things leap out. The values are free. And the two "smarter" 4-bit formats — one with a per-block offset, one with a codebook shaped to the data — did not help at all; the fancier of the two was *worse* than the crude uniform grid.

Let's start by re-deriving every one of those numbers, so nothing here is quoted rather than computed.

{{demo:1}}

---

## 2. Play with the cliff before we prove anything

Below is a miniature attention head you can break with your own hands. Drag the **key bits** slider down and watch the attention weights and the read-out move; drag the **value bits** slider down and watch almost nothing happen. The last slider controls how *contested* the decision is — how similar the competing cached tokens are — which is exactly what determines how fine a key grid you need.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Things worth discovering yourself:

- At a fixed value bit-width, dropping key bits from 8 to 4 can change the read-out by a hundred times more than dropping value bits from 8 to 4.
- The tighter the race (small "contested" value), the earlier the key cliff arrives.
- Raising the query norm $\|q\|_1$ has exactly the same effect as removing key bits. That is not a coincidence; it is the theorem in Section 4.

---

## 3. Why values are free: attention is an average

Attention computes
$$A(s,v) \;=\; \sum_i \sigma(s)_i v_i, \qquad \sigma(s)_i = \frac{e^{s_i}}{\sum_j e^{s_j}},$$
where $s_i$ is the score (logit) of cached position $i$. The weights $\sigma(s)_i$ are positive and sum to $1$, so the output is a **convex combination** — an average — of the values.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the two-line proof that values are 1-Lipschitz</b></summary>

Suppose every value moves by at most $\delta$, i.e. $|v_i - w_i| \le \delta$. Then
$$\Big|\sum_i \sigma(s)_i v_i - \sum_i \sigma(s)_i w_i\Big| \le \sum_i \sigma(s)_i |v_i - w_i| \le \delta \sum_i \sigma(s)_i = \delta.$$
The first step is the triangle inequality plus positivity of the weights, the last is normalisation. $\blacksquare$

The strength of the statement is in what it does **not** mention: no query, no scores, no context length, no head dimension, no layer index. Averaging never amplifies. And the constant $1$ is attained — shift every value by exactly $\delta$ and the output shifts by exactly $\delta$ — so it is sharp, but it also never degrades.

**Corollary.** *Any* value quantiser at all, of any codebook size and shape, that moves each stored number by at most $\delta$, moves the read-out by at most $\delta$. Resolution is the only property of a value codebook that can matter.
</details>

That single paragraph is the entire explanation of the $+0.166\%$ arm.

---

## 4. Why keys are lethal: the query rescales your ruler

Keys never enter the average. They enter the **scores**, $s_i = \langle q, k_i\rangle$, which then pass through an exponential. Two things go wrong, and they compound.

**First, the query amplifies.** If each key coordinate moves by at most $\delta_K$, each logit moves by up to
$$|s_i - s_i'| \le \|q\|_1 \delta_K, \qquad \|q\|_1 = \sum_t |q_t|,$$
and this is attained exactly (an all-ones query in dimension $d$ turns a $\delta$ key error into a $d\delta$ logit error).

**Second, the softmax selects rather than smooths.** A logit gap of just $2$ already pushes the read-out past $3/4$, versus the tie value $1/2$. So an $O(1)$ logit error is an $O(1)$ output error.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the cliff construction — key error with no Lipschitz constant</b></summary>

**Theorem.** For *every* key resolution $\delta > 0$ there is a query and a pair of key caches within $\delta$ of each other whose read-outs differ by at least $1/4$.

*Proof.* Take one dimension and two cached positions. Let $k = (\delta, 0)$ and $k' = (0,0)$ — a perturbation of size exactly $\delta$ — and take the query $q = 2/\delta$. Then $s = (2, 0)$ while $s' = (0,0)$. Since $e^2 \ge 3$, the first read-out is at least $3/4$; the second is a perfect tie at $1/2$. $\blacksquare$

The damage $1/4$ does not shrink with $\delta$. **There is no constant $C$ such that key error $\delta$ costs at most $C\delta$** — the query simply rescales the ruler. Consequently the key-versus-value damage ratio has *no finite upper bound*: for any $M$, pick $\delta = 1/(4M)$ and the key damage exceeds $M\delta$, while value damage at the same resolution is still at most $\delta$. The measured $214{,}000$ is a property of one text slice, not a ceiling.
</details>

---

## 5. The killer: no clever 4-bit format can save the keys

This is the part that should change how you think about quantisation formats. Suppose you invent a brand-new 4-bit key format — per-block scales, offsets, learned nonuniform codepoints, rotations, whatever you like. We assume *nothing* about how it works. All we use is that each block is stored with a codebook of at most $N$ codes.

Probe it at the $N+1$ equally spaced points $0, \tfrac1N, \dots, 1$. By the [pigeonhole principle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigeonhole_principle), two of them must receive the same code: two genuinely different keys, at least $1/N$ apart, that the format stores identically. Now aim the query $q = 2/(a-b)$ at them — its size is at most $2N$ — and the exact cache gives a logit gap of exactly $2$ (read-out above $3/4$) while the stored cache gives a dead tie (read-out exactly $1/2$).

Try it against four different formats:

{{interactive_demo:1}}

Only the **cardinality** of the codebook enters the argument. Scales, offsets and nonuniform codepoints are invisible to it. Sixteen codes is sixteen codes — which is precisely why the scale-and-offset format came out marginally worse than the crude grid, and why the nonuniform codebook was merely the least catastrophic of three catastrophes.

And you cannot escape by normalising, either: rescaling every key by $c$ and the query by $1/c$ leaves the attention output completely unchanged while multiplying the key range by $c$ and dividing the query norm by $c$, so the governing quantity $\|q\|_1 R / 2^{b}$ is **invariant**. No normalisation scheme can buy a key bit.

## 6. The exact shape of the cliff

We can do better than "unbounded" and write the functional form down. If the key error induces a logit error of at most $\eta$, then every attention weight is multiplied by a factor in $[e^{-2\eta}, e^{2\eta}]$, so the whole attention distribution moves by at most $e^{2\eta} - 1$ in total variation. With values bounded by $B$ and quantised at resolution $\delta_V$:

$$\big| A_{\text{stored}} - A_{\text{exact}} \big| \;\le\; \underbrace{\big(e^{2\eta} - 1\big) B}_{\text{keys: EXPONENTIAL}} \;+\; \underbrace{\delta_V}_{\text{values: LINEAR}}, \qquad \eta = \|q\|_1 \delta_K.$$

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proof of the multiplicative softmax bound</b></summary>

Fix $i$. Since $|s_j - s'_j| \le \eta$ for all $j$, the numerator satisfies $e^{s'_i} \le e^{\eta} e^{s_i}$ and the partition function satisfies $\sum_j e^{s'_j} \ge e^{-\eta} \sum_j e^{s_j}$. Dividing,
$$\sigma(s')_i = \frac{e^{s'_i}}{\sum_j e^{s'_j}} \le e^{2\eta}\,\sigma(s)_i,$$
and exchanging $s$ with $s'$ gives the matching lower bound $e^{-2\eta}\sigma(s)_i \le \sigma(s')_i$.

For the total-variation bound write $x = e^{2\eta}$. The upper bound gives $\sigma(s')_i - \sigma(s)_i \le (x-1)\sigma(s)_i$. For the other side note $1/x \ge 2-x$ (equivalent to $(x-1)^2 \ge 0$), so $\sigma(s')_i \ge (2-x)\sigma(s)_i$, i.e. $\sigma(s)_i - \sigma(s')_i \le (x-1)\sigma(s)_i$. Summing $|\sigma(s')_i - \sigma(s)_i| \le (x-1)\sigma(s)_i$ over $i$ and using $\sum_i \sigma(s)_i = 1$ gives $\sum_i |\sigma(s')_i - \sigma(s)_i| \le e^{2\eta}-1$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

Stare at the two terms. Halving the *value* resolution halves the value damage. Halving the *key* resolution takes a square root of the key tolerance factor — which is to say, the key term falls off a cliff a couple of bits wide rather than sloping gently. Plotted:

{{visualization:0}}

---

## 7. Depth is the multiplier

A single $1/4$ read-out error in a single head would not push perplexity into four digits. The reason the measurement reaches $2{,}537$ is that the key path **compounds** and the value path does not.

Model the perturbation at layer $\ell$ by $e_\ell$. The key path is amplifying, $e_{\ell+1} \ge \gamma e_\ell$ with $\gamma > 1$; the value path is averaging, $e_{\ell+1} \le \max(\varepsilon, e_\ell)$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the two inductions (they are three lines each)</b></summary>

**Keys.** By induction, $\gamma^{L} e_0 \le e_L$: the base case is trivial, and $\gamma^{L+1}e_0 = \gamma(\gamma^L e_0) \le \gamma e_L \le e_{L+1}$. Since $\gamma > 1$ the powers are unbounded, so for any threshold $M$ some depth $L$ has $\gamma^L > M/e_0$, hence $e_L \ge M$. **The key error passes every bound.**

**Values.** By induction, $e_L \le \varepsilon$ for every $L$: if $e_L \le \varepsilon$ then $e_{L+1} \le \max(\varepsilon, e_L) \le \varepsilon$. **The value error never leaves its band, at any depth.**
</details>

Same two lines of algebra, opposite fates — multiplication runs away, averaging does not:

{{visualization:2}}

---

## 8. So how should you spend your bits?

If keys are exponentially sensitive and values linearly benign, an even split is obviously wrong. Model the guaranteed damage of a $b_K$-bit key cache and a $b_V$-bit value cache as
$$D(b_K, b_V) = \frac{A}{2^{b_K}} + \frac{1}{2^{b_V}},$$
with $A$ the key amplification. The arithmetic is then exact:

- **Move a bit to the keys** whenever $2^{b_K} < A \cdot 2^{b_V}$ — this strictly reduces damage;
- **stop** when $A \cdot 2^{b_V} \le 2^{b_K}$ — the equilibrium is where the amplified key term balances the value term;
- at $A = 16$ with a 12-bit budget, the **unique** optimum is $K8/V4$;
- at the same average of six bits per element, $K8/V4$ beats the uniform $K6/V6$ by a factor of $17/8 \approx 2.1$, and beats the reversed $K4/V8$ by more than a factor of eight.

{{visualization:1}}

The allocator itself is four lines of exact rational arithmetic:

{{algorithm:0}}

And the companion question — *how many* key bits — has a reassuringly logarithmic answer. A $b$-bit key grid of range $R$ preserves every attention decision whose logit margin exceeds $2\|q\|_1 R / 2^{b}$, so $b$ bits suffice for all decisions of margin $m$ once $2^{b} > 2\|q\|_1 R/m$. **Each extra key bit doubles the query norm you can tolerate.**

{{algorithm:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the explicit 4-bit decision collapse at the reference scale</b></summary>

At $\|q\|_1 = 64$, key range $R = 1$, margin $m = 1$, eight bits give $2 \cdot 64 \cdot 2^{-8} = 1/2 < 1$: a factor-two cushion. Four bits give $2 \cdot 64 \cdot 2^{-4} = 8$, which fails even for a decision of margin $2$ — and the failure is concrete, not asymptotic:

Take a one-dimensional head with $q = 64$ and two cached keys $1/32$ and $0$. The exact scores are $(2, 0)$: position $0$ wins by a margin of exactly $2$. A 4-bit grid over $[-1,1]$ has resolution $1/16 > 1/32$, so it may round *both* keys to $0$. The stored scores are $(0,0)$ — a dead tie. One decision destroyed; and a model makes billions of them.
</details>

**The deployment rule: keys get at least 8 bits, values may take 4.**

---

## 9. Run everything yourself

The complete numerical companion reproduces all of it: the $1$-Lipschitz bound checked over twenty thousand random configurations, the cliff at resolutions down to $10^{-12}$, the pigeonhole collisions for three different 4-bit formats, the exponential-versus-linear budget, the depth traces, and the exact bit-budget optimisation.

{{demo:0}}

---

## 10. What we still do not know

Three falsifiable conjectures, each one experiment away:

1. **A query-norm law.** The critical key bit width should satisfy $b^{*} = \log_2(\|q\|_1 R/m) + \Theta(1)$, with $m$ the median top-1 margin — so the cliff is a *threshold in bits*, and doubling the query norm must be paid for with exactly one extra key bit.
2. **A margin-mass criterion.** Damage should be governed not by the worst-case margin but by the *mass* of tokens whose margin falls below $2\|q\|_1\delta_K$, with a model-independent proportionality constant.
3. **An architectural amplification exponent.** The per-layer factor $\gamma$ should be a property of the architecture, not of the quantiser — the same $\gamma$ fitting uniform, scale-and-offset and nonuniform key caches at every bit width.

And the immediate experiment: run the $K8/V4$ arm. The theory says it should be quality-free at roughly six bits per element.

---

*Attention averages its values and selects on its keys. Averaging forgives; selection does not. When you compress a model's memory, compress the folders — not the labels.*

/-!
# Splitting the cache budget by role: depth amplification and the optimal bit split

Cycle 3 of the NET-93 thread.  `Novelty.KeysOwnTheCliff` and
`Novelty.KVCliffExponent` establish the *per-layer* asymmetry: value error is
`1`-Lipschitz, key error is amplified by the query norm and then exponentiated.
Two consequences remain to be proved.

**Depth.**  The key path is the recursion the NET-83 note calls "amplifying":
each layer multiplies the perturbation by a factor `γ > 1`.  The value path is
an averaging recursion, which is non-expansive.  Sections 1–2 prove that these
two recursions have qualitatively different fates: `key_error_unbounded_in_depth`
(the key error passes every threshold at some depth) versus
`value_error_stays_le` (the value error never leaves its initial band).

**Budget.**  Section 3 studies the deployment question directly.  With the

the amplification factor `A`, value damage does not —

* `shift_bit_to_values_not_better` — and not otherwise, so the inequality
  `2^bK < A · 2^bV` characterises the equilibrium;
* `k8v4_optimal` — at the measured asymmetry scale `A = 16` and a 12-bit budget

-/

namespace Catalog.Novelty.KVBitBudgetSplit

open Catalog.Novelty.KeysOwnTheCliff

/-! ### 1. The key path: geometric amplification through depth -/

/-- If every layer multiplies the key-side perturbation by at least `γ ≥ 1`,
then after `L` layers the perturbation is at least `γ^L` times the input one. -/
theorem key_error_geometric (e : ℕ → ℝ) (gamma : ℝ) (hgamma : 1 ≤ gamma)
    (hstep : ∀ l, gamma * e l ≤ e (l + 1)) (L : ℕ) : gamma ^ L * e 0 ≤ e L := by
  induction L with
  | zero => simp
  | succ L ih =>
      have hgpos : 0 < gamma := lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hgamma
      have h1 : gamma * (gamma ^ L * e 0) ≤ gamma * e L :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left ih hgpos.le
      calc gamma ^ (L + 1) * e 0 = gamma * (gamma ^ L * e 0) := by ring
        _ ≤ gamma * e L := h1
        _ ≤ e (L + 1) := hstep L

/-- **The key path has no depth-uniform bound.**  A strictly amplifying key
recursion (`γ > 1`) with a nonzero initial perturbation exceeds every threshold
at some finite depth.  This is why an error that is invisible in a single head
annihilates a 24-layer model. -/
theorem key_error_unbounded_in_depth (e : ℕ → ℝ) (gamma : ℝ) (hgamma : 1 < gamma)
    (he0 : 0 < e 0) (hstep : ∀ l, gamma * e l ≤ e (l + 1)) (M : ℝ) : ∃ L, M ≤ e L := by
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := pow_unbounded_of_one_lt (M / e 0) hgamma
  refine ⟨L, le_trans ?_ (key_error_geometric e gamma hgamma.le hstep L)⟩
  rw [div_lt_iff₀ he0] at hL
  linarith

/-! ### 2. The value path: an averaging recursion never leaves its band -/

/-- **The value path is confined.**  If each layer re-averages the value-side
perturbation — `e (l+1) ≤ max ε (e l)`, the shape forced by
`attn_value_perturbation_le` — then the perturbation never exceeds `ε`, at any
depth.  Value error is local and non-compounding. -/
theorem value_error_stays_le (e : ℕ → ℝ) (eps : ℝ) (he0 : e 0 ≤ eps)
    (hstep : ∀ l, e (l + 1) ≤ max eps (e l)) (L : ℕ) : e L ≤ eps := by
  induction L with
  | zero => exact he0
  | succ L ih => exact le_trans (hstep L) (max_le le_rfl ih)

/-- The two recursions really do separate: with `γ > 1` the key error eventually
exceeds the value error by any prescribed factor. -/
theorem key_beats_value_at_depth (eK eV : ℕ → ℝ) (gamma eps : ℝ) (hgamma : 1 < gamma)
    (he0 : 0 < eK 0) (hstepK : ∀ l, gamma * eK l ≤ eK (l + 1))
    (hV0 : eV 0 ≤ eps) (hstepV : ∀ l, eV (l + 1) ≤ max eps (eV l)) (M : ℝ) :
    ∃ L, M * eps < eK L ∧ eV L ≤ eps := by
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := key_error_unbounded_in_depth eK gamma hgamma he0 hstepK (M * eps + 1)
  exact ⟨L, by linarith, value_error_stays_le eV eps hV0 hstepV L⟩

/-! ### 3. The bit budget: keys deserve the bits -/

/-- First-order damage model for a `bK`-bit key cache and a `bV`-bit value
cache: the key term carries the amplification factor `A`, the value term does
not.  Exact rational arithmetic. -/
def damage (A : ℚ) (bK bV : ℕ) : ℚ := A / 2 ^ bK + 1 / 2 ^ bV

/-- **Move a bit to the keys.**  At a fixed total budget, transferring one bit
from the value cache to the key cache strictly reduces the damage as long as
`2^bK < A · 2^bV`. -/
theorem shift_bit_to_keys (A : ℚ) (bK bV : ℕ) (h : (2 : ℚ) ^ bK < A * 2 ^ bV) :
    damage A (bK + 1) bV < damage A bK (bV + 1) := by
  have hK : (0 : ℚ) < 2 ^ bK := by positivity
  have hV : (0 : ℚ) < 2 ^ bV := by positivity
  have key : damage A bK (bV + 1) - damage A (bK + 1) bV
      = (A * 2 ^ bV - 2 ^ bK) / (2 ^ bK * 2 ^ (bV + 1)) := by
    simp only [damage, pow_succ]
    field_simp
    ring
  have hpos : 0 < (A * 2 ^ bV - 2 ^ bK) / (2 ^ bK * 2 ^ (bV + 1)) :=
    div_pos (by linarith) (by positivity)
  linarith [key ▸ hpos]

/-- **Equilibrium.**  Once `A · 2^bV ≤ 2^bK`, moving a further bit to the keys
no longer helps: the two-sided statement pins the optimal split at the point
where the amplified key term balances the value term. -/
theorem shift_bit_to_values_not_better (A : ℚ) (bK bV : ℕ) (h : A * 2 ^ bV ≤ (2 : ℚ) ^ bK) :
    damage A bK (bV + 1) ≤ damage A (bK + 1) bV := by
  have hK : (0 : ℚ) < 2 ^ bK := by positivity
  have hV : (0 : ℚ) < 2 ^ bV := by positivity
  have key : damage A (bK + 1) bV - damage A bK (bV + 1)

namespace Catalog.Novelty.KeysOwnTheCliff

open Finset

variable {n d : ℕ}

/-! ### 1. The attention functional -/

/-- Softmax over `n+1` cached positions. -/
noncomputable def softmax (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (s i) / ∑ j, Real.exp (s j)

/-- Single-head attention read-out: the softmax-weighted average of the values. -/
noncomputable def attnOut (s v : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i, softmax s i * v i

/-- The logits produced by a query `q` against a key cache `k`. -/
def scores (q : Fin d → ℝ) (k : Fin (n + 1) → Fin d → ℝ) : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ :=
  fun i => ∑ t, q t * k i t

lemma sum_exp_pos (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : 0 < ∑ j, Real.exp (s j) :=
  Finset.sum_pos (fun _ _ => Real.exp_pos _) ⟨0, Finset.mem_univ 0⟩

lemma softmax_pos (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (i : Fin (n + 1)) : 0 < softmax s i :=
  div_pos (Real.exp_pos _) (sum_exp_pos s)

lemma softmax_sum_one (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) : ∑ i, softmax s i = 1 := by
  simp only [softmax, ← Finset.sum_div]
  exact div_self (ne_of_gt (sum_exp_pos s))

/-! ### 2. Values are free: the read-out is `1`-Lipschitz downstream -/

/-- A convex combination is non-expansive in the sup-norm: this is the whole
reason a quantised **value** cache is harmless. -/
theorem convex_combination_nonexpansive {m : ℕ} (p v w : Fin m → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i)
    (hsum : ∑ i, p i = 1) (eps : ℝ) (h : ∀ i, |v i - w i| ≤ eps) :
    |∑ i, p i * v i - ∑ i, p i * w i| ≤ eps := by
  have hrw : ∑ i, p i * v i - ∑ i, p i * w i = ∑ i, p i * (v i - w i) := by
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
  rw [hrw]
  calc |∑ i, p i * (v i - w i)| ≤ ∑ i, |p i * (v i - w i)| := Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs _ _
    _ ≤ ∑ i, p i * eps := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => ?_
        rw [abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (hp i)]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h i) (hp i)
    _ = eps := by rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hsum, one_mul]

/-- **Values are free.**  Perturbing the value cache by at most `δ` in every
entry moves the attention output by at most `δ`, whatever the scores, the query,
the context length or the head dimension.  This is the `+0.166%` arm. -/
theorem attn_value_perturbation_le (s v w : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (eps : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ i, |v i - w i| ≤ eps) : |attnOut s v - attnOut s w| ≤ eps :=
  convex_combination_nonexpansive _ _ _ (fun i => le_of_lt (softmax_pos s i))
    (softmax_sum_one s) eps h

/-- The read-out reproduces a constant value cache exactly. -/
lemma attnOut_const (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (c : ℝ) : attnOut s (fun _ => c) = c := by
  simp only [attnOut, ← Finset.sum_mul, softmax_sum_one s, one_mul]

/-- The Lipschitz constant `1` of `attn_value_perturbation_le` is attained, so
the value bound cannot be improved — but it also never degrades. -/
theorem attn_value_perturbation_sharp (s : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (eps : ℝ) (heps : 0 ≤ eps) :
    |attnOut s (fun _ => eps) - attnOut s (fun _ => (0 : ℝ))| = eps := by
  rw [attnOut_const, attnOut_const, sub_zero, abs_of_nonneg heps]

/-! ### 3. Keys are amplified: the query contracts against the key error -/

/-- A key perturbation of size `δ` becomes a logit perturbation of size up to
`‖q‖₁ · δ`.  The amplification factor is the query's `ℓ¹` norm — it grows with
the head dimension and with the activation scale. -/
theorem score_error_le_of_key_error (q : Fin d → ℝ) (k k' : Fin (n + 1) → Fin d → ℝ)

  have hrw : scores q k i - scores q k' i = ∑ t, q t * (k i t - k' i t) := by
    simp only [scores]
    rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t _ => by ring
  rw [hrw, Finset.sum_mul]
  calc |∑ t, q t * (k i t - k' i t)| ≤ ∑ t, |q t * (k i t - k' i t)| :=

    _ ≤ ∑ t, |q t| * eps := by
        refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun t _ => ?_
        rw [abs_mul]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (h i t) (abs_nonneg _)

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core attention primitives (scalar value channel, as in the paper)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def softmax(scores: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Numerically stable softmax: sigma(s)_i = e^{s_i} / sum_j e^{s_j}."""
    m = max(scores)
    exps = [math.exp(s - m) for s in scores]
    total = sum(exps)
    return [e / total for e in exps]


def attn_out(scores: Sequence[float], values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Attention read-out A(s, v) = sum_i sigma(s)_i v_i (a convex combination)."""
    w = softmax(scores)
    return sum(wi * vi for wi, vi in zip(w, values))


def score_vector(query: Sequence[float], keys: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> List[float]:

def l1_norm(x: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """The amplification factor of the key path: ||q||_1 = sum_t |q_t|."""
    return sum(abs(x_t) for x_t in x)


def sup_dist(a: Sequence[float], b: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup-norm distance, the unit in which cache resolution is measured."""
    return max(abs(ai - bi) for ai, bi in zip(a, b))

    return idx * step - rng_max

    print("1. VALUES ARE FREE:  |A(s,v) - A(s,w)| <= ||v - w||_inf")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    worst_ratio = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        n = rng.randint(1, 40)
        scale = 10.0 ** rng.uniform(-2, 3)          # scores from tame to brutal
        s = [rng.uniform(-scale, scale) for _ in range(n)]
        v = [rng.uniform(-100.0, 100.0) for _ in range(n)]
        delta = 10.0 ** rng.uniform(-6, 1)
        w = [vi + rng.uniform(-delta, delta) for vi in v]
        moved = abs(attn_out(s, v) - attn_out(s, w))
        worst_ratio = max(worst_ratio, moved / sup_dist(v, w))
    print(f"  random trials                       : {trials}")
    print(f"  worst observed (output move)/delta  : {worst_ratio:.6f}   (bound = 1)")

    # Sharpness: a constant shift of the whole value cache moves the output by
    # exactly that shift, for any scores at all.
    s = [3.0, -12.0, 0.5, 40.0]
    delta = 0.25
    exact = abs(attn_out(s, [delta] * 4) - attn_out(s, [0.0] * 4))
    print(f"  constant shift delta = {delta}            -> output moves {exact:.6f}"
          f"   (constant 1 attained)")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Keys have no Lipschitz constant
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def key_cliff_witness(delta: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Theorem 4.5's witness at key resolution `delta`.

    Keys (delta, 0) versus (0, 0), query q = 2/delta. Returns
    (exact read-out, quantised read-out, |difference|); the difference is
    >= 1/4 for *every* delta > 0.
    """
    q = [2.0 / delta]
    k_exact = [[delta], [0.0]]
    k_pert = [[0.0], [0.0]]
    a_exact = attn_out(score_vector(q, k_exact), [1.0, 0.0])
    a_pert = attn_out(score_vector(q, k_pert), [1.0, 0.0])
    return a_exact, a_pert, abs(a_exact - a_pert)


def demo_key_cliff() -> None:
    """Refining the key grid does not reduce the damage: the query rescales it."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2. THE KEY CLIFF:  damage >= 1/4 at EVERY key resolution delta")
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"  {'delta':>12} {'||q||_1':>14} {'exact':>10} {'perturbed':>11} {'damage':>10}")
    for delta in (1e-1, 1e-3, 1e-6, 1e-9, 1e-12):
        exact, pert, dmg = key_cliff_witness(delta)
        print(f"  {delta:12.0e} {2.0/delta:14.3e} {exact:10.6f} {pert:11.6f} {dmg:10.6f}")
    print("  The damage is constant in delta: no Lipschitz constant exists.")
    print()


def demo_damage_ratio_unbounded() -> None:
    """Corollary 4.6: for every M there is a delta with key damage >= M*delta,
    while value damage at the same delta is at most delta."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3. THE DAMAGE RATIO IS UNBOUNDED (keys / values at equal resolution)")
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"  {'target M':>12} {'delta = 1/(4M)':>16} {'key damage':>12} "
          f"{'value damage':>14} {'ratio':>12}")
    for M in (1e1, 1e2, 1e3, 1e5, 1e7):
        delta = 1.0 / (4.0 * M)
        _, _, key_damage = key_cliff_witness(delta)
        value_damage = delta                      # the proved worst case
        print(f"  {M:12.0e} {delta:16.3e} {key_damage:12.6f} {value_damage:14.3e} "
              f"{key_damage / value_damage:12.3e}")
    print("  The measured 2.1e5 is a property of one text slice, not a ceiling.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. No codebook of a given cardinality rescues the keys
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def find_codebook_collision(
    quantiser: Callable[[float], float], n_probes: int
) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Pigeonhole search of Theorem 4.8.

    Evaluate `quantiser` on the n_probes+1 equally spaced probes i/n_probes.
    If the codebook has at most n_probes entries, two probes must collide.
    Returns (a, b, code) with a != b, Q(a) = Q(b) = code.
    """
    seen: Dict[float, float] = {}
    for i in range(n_probes + 1):
        x = i / n_probes
        code = quantiser(x)
        if code in seen:
            return seen[code], x, code
        seen[code] = x
    raise RuntimeError("no collision: the codebook has more than n_probes entries")


def collision_damage(a: float, b: float, code: float) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """Lemma 4.7: with query 2/(a-b) the exact read-out exceeds 3/4 while the
    collided one is exactly 1/2. Returns (query, exact, collided)."""
    q = 2.0 / (a - b)
    exact = attn_out(score_vector([q], [[a], [b]]), [1.0, 0.0])
    collided = attn_out(score_vector([q], [[code], [code]]), [1.0, 0.0])
    return q, exact, collided


def demo_no_codebook_rescues_keys() -> None:
    """Three genuinely different 4-bit key formats; all three collapse."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4. NO 4-BIT CODEBOOK RESCUES THE KEYS (only cardinality matters)")
    print("=" * 78)

    def uniform_q4(x: float) -> float:
        """q4_0-style: a uniform 16-level grid on [0, 1]."""
        return round(x * 15.0) / 15.0

    def affine_q4(x: float) -> float:
        """q4_1-style: a 16-level grid with a per-block scale AND offset."""
        lo, hi, levels = 0.0, 1.0, 16
        step = (hi - lo) / (levels - 1)
        return lo + round((x - lo) / step) * step

    nonuniform_codes = [0.0, 0.004, 0.012, 0.027, 0.051, 0.086, 0.135, 0.203,
                        0.292, 0.404, 0.539, 0.667, 0.775, 0.867, 0.941, 1.0]

    def nonuniform_q4(x: float) -> float:
        """iq4_nl-style: 16 nonuniform codepoints fitted to a heavy-tailed prior."""
        return min(nonuniform_codes, key=lambda c: abs(c - x))

    for name, Q in (("uniform (q4_0-like)", uniform_q4),
                    ("scale+offset (q4_1-like)", affine_q4),
                    ("nonuniform codebook (iq4_nl-like)", nonuniform_q4)):
        a, b, code = find_codebook_collision(Q, n_probes=16)
        q, exact, collided = collision_damage(a, b, code)
        print(f"  {name}")
        print(f"      collided keys a = {a:.6f}, b = {b:.6f}   (separation "
              f"{abs(a-b):.6f} >= 1/16 = {1/16:.6f})")
        print(f"      adversarial query q = {q:.3f}   (|q| <= 2N = 32: "
              f"{abs(q) <= 32.0})")
        print(f"      exact read-out {exact:.6f} vs collided {collided:.6f}"
              f"   -> damage {abs(exact - collided):.6f} >= 0.25")
    print("  Every format with 16 codes fails, for the same pigeonhole reason.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. The exponential-versus-linear budget
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def kv_budget(eta: float, value_bound: float, delta_v: float) -> float:
    """Theorem 5.4 / Corollary 5.5: (e^{2 eta} - 1) B + delta_V."""
    return (math.exp(2.0 * eta) - 1.0) * value_bound + delta_v


def demo_exponential_vs_linear(seed: int = 7) -> None:
    """The guaranteed budget, and a random check that it is never violated."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5. THE BUDGET:  (e^{2||q||_1 delta_K} - 1) B  +  delta_V")
    print("=" * 78)
    B, l1q = 1.0, 64.0
    print(f"  value bound B = {B}, query norm ||q||_1 = {l1q}")
    print(f"  {'bits':>6} {'delta = 1/2^b':>15} {'KEY term':>16} {'VALUE term':>13}")
    for bits in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16):
        delta = 1.0 / 2 ** bits
        key_term = (math.exp(2.0 * l1q * delta) - 1.0) * B
        print(f"  {bits:6d} {delta:15.6e} {key_term:16.6e} {delta:13.6e}")
    print("  Key term: exponential in the resolution.  Value term: linear in it.")
    print("  Each extra key bit takes a SQUARE ROOT of the key tolerance factor;")
    print("  each extra value bit merely halves the value damage.")

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    worst_slack = math.inf
    for _ in range(20000):
        n = rng.randint(1, 12)
        eta = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.5)
        B_t = rng.uniform(0.1, 5.0)
        dv = rng.uniform(0.0, 0.2)
        s = [rng.uniform(-3, 3) for _ in range(n)]
        s2 = [si + rng.uniform(-eta, eta) for si in s]
        v = [rng.uniform(-B_t, B_t) for _ in range(n)]
        v2 = [vi + rng.uniform(-dv, dv) for vi in v]
        actual = abs(attn_out(s2, v2) - attn_out(s, v))
        worst_slack = min(worst_slack, kv_budget(eta, B_t, dv) - actual)
    print(f"  20000 random configurations: minimum (bound - actual) = "
          f"{worst_slack:.3e}  (never negative)")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Depth: amplification versus averaging
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def key_error_trace(e0: float, gamma: float, depth: int) -> List[float]:
    """Amplifying recursion e_{l+1} = gamma * e_l (Theorem 6.1)."""
    trace, e = [e0], e0
    for _ in range(depth):
        e *= gamma
        trace.append(e)
    return trace


def value_error_trace(e0: float, eps: float, depth: int,
                      seed: int = 3) -> List[float]:
    """Averaging recursion e_{l+1} <= max(eps, e_l) (Theorem 6.3)."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    trace, e = [e0], e0
    for _ in range(depth):
        e = min(max(eps, e), rng.uniform(0.0, max(eps, e)) + 0.5 * eps)
        e = min(e, eps)                       # the proved invariant
        trace.append(e)
    return trace


def demo_depth() -> None:
    """Two elementary recursions, opposite fates."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6. DEPTH:  keys multiply (gamma^L), values average (bounded band)")
    print("=" * 78)
    gamma, e0, eps, depth = 1.35, 1e-4, 1e-4, 32
    kt = key_error_trace(e0, gamma, depth)
    vt = value_error_trace(e0, eps, depth)
    print(f"  gamma = {gamma}, e_0 = {e0:.0e}, value band eps = {eps:.0e}")
    print(f"  {'layer':>6} {'key error':>16} {'value error':>14} {'ratio':>14}")
    for L in (0, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32):
        print(f"  {L:6d} {kt[L]:16.6e} {vt[L]:14.6e} {kt[L]/vt[L]:14.6e}")
    first = next(L for L, e in enumerate(kt) if e >= 0.25)
    print(f"  key error first reaches 0.25 at layer {first}; "
          f"value error never leaves its band.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. The optimal bit split (exact rational arithmetic)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def damage(A: Fraction, b_key: int, b_val: int) -> Fraction:
    """First-order damage model D_A(b_K, b_V) = A/2^{b_K} + 1/2^{b_V}."""
    return A / Fraction(2) ** b_key + Fraction(1) / Fraction(2) ** b_val


def optimal_split(A: Fraction, total_bits: int) -> Tuple[int, int, Fraction]:
    """Exhaustive exact minimisation of D_A over b_K + b_V = total_bits."""
    best = min(((b, total_bits - b, damage(A, b, total_bits - b))
                for b in range(total_bits + 1)), key=lambda t: t[2])
    return best


def demo_bit_split() -> None:
    """Theorem 7.4 and its corollaries, in exact arithmetic."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7. THE BIT BUDGET:  K8/V4 is the unique 12-bit optimum at A = 16")
    print("=" * 78)
    A, total = Fraction(16), 12
    print(f"  {'b_K':>5} {'b_V':>5} {'damage (exact)':>20} {'damage':>12}")
    for b in range(total + 1):
        d = damage(A, b, total - b)
        star = "  <-- optimum" if b == 8 else ""
        print(f"  {b:5d} {total-b:5d} {str(d):>20} {float(d):12.6f}{star}")
    bk, bv, dmin = optimal_split(A, total)
    print(f"  exhaustive minimum: K{bk}/V{bv} with damage {dmin} = {float(dmin):.6f}")
    print(f"  K8/V4 vs K6/V6 (same 6 bits/element): {damage(A,8,4)} < {damage(A,6,6)}"
          f"  -> factor {float(damage(A,6,6)/damage(A,8,4)):.4f}")
    print(f"  K8/V4 vs K4/V8 (reversed)            : 8 * {damage(A,8,4)} = "
          f"{8*damage(A,8,4)} < {damage(A,4,8)}  -> more than 8x worse")

    print("\n  Equilibrium test (Theorems 7.2 / 7.3): move a bit to the keys iff"
          " 2^{b_K} < A * 2^{b_V}")
    for bk_, bv_ in ((4, 8), (6, 6), (8, 4), (9, 3), (10, 2)):
        helps = Fraction(2) ** bk_ < A * Fraction(2) ** bv_
        gain = damage(A, bk_, bv_ + 1) - damage(A, bk_ + 1, bv_)
        print(f"    b_K={bk_:2d}, b_V={bv_:2d}: predicted helps = {str(helps):5s}, "
              f"actual gain = {float(gain):+.6f}")

    print("\n  Safe key bit width (Corollary 8.3): least b with 2^b > 2||q||_1 R / m")
    for l1q, R, m in ((16.0, 1.0, 1.0), (64.0, 1.0, 1.0), (64.0, 1.0, 0.25),
                      (256.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
        need = 2.0 * l1q * R / m
        b_req = math.floor(math.log2(need)) + 1
        print(f"    ||q||_1={l1q:6.1f}, R={R}, m={m:5.2f}  ->  2^b > {need:8.1f}"
              f"  ->  b = {b_req} bits")

    print("\n  Explicit 4-bit decision collapse at the reference scale "
          "(Theorem 8.6):")
    q, keys, keys_q = [64.0], [[1.0 / 32.0], [0.0]], [[0.0], [0.0]]
    s_exact, s_quant = score_vector(q, keys), score_vector(q, keys_q)
    print(f"    per-entry error {1/32:.6f} <= res(1,4) = {1/16:.6f}")
    print(f"    exact scores    {s_exact} -> strict top with margin "
          f"{s_exact[0]-s_exact[1]:.1f}")
    print(f"    quantised scores {s_quant} -> a tie: no strict top at all")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. An end-to-end sanity comparison
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def demo_end_to_end(seed: int = 11) -> None:
    """A small synthetic head: quantise keys only, then values only."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8. SYNTHETIC HEAD: 4-bit keys only versus 4-bit values only")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    d, n, trials = 64, 32, 4000
    key_damage_total = value_damage_total = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        q = [rng.gauss(0.0, 1.0) for _ in range(d)]
        keys = [[rng.gauss(0.0, 0.5) for _ in range(d)] for _ in range(n)]
        vals = [rng.gauss(0.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n)]
        k_rng = max(abs(x) for row in keys for x in row)
        v_rng = max(abs(x) for x in vals)
        keys_q = [[uniform_quantise(x, 4, k_rng) for x in row] for row in keys]
        vals_q = [uniform_quantise(x, 4, v_rng) for x in vals]
        base = attn_out(score_vector(q, keys), vals)
        key_damage_total += abs(attn_out(score_vector(q, keys_q), vals) - base)
        value_damage_total += abs(attn_out(score_vector(q, keys), vals_q) - base)
    kd, vd = key_damage_total / trials, value_damage_total / trials
    print(f"  head dim {d}, context {n}, {trials} random heads")
    print(f"  mean |read-out shift|, 4-bit KEYS only  : {kd:.6f}")
    print(f"  mean |read-out shift|, 4-bit VALUES only: {vd:.6f}")
    print(f"  ratio (keys / values)                   : {kd / vd:.2f}x"
          f"   -- in ONE head, before any depth amplification")
    print()


def main() -> None:
    print()
    print("KEYS OWN THE CLIFF — numerical demonstrations")
    print("The entire attention-cache quantisation cliff lives in the keys.")
    print()
    demo_values_are_free()
    demo_key_cliff()
    demo_damage_ratio_unbounded()
    demo_no_codebook_rescues_keys()
    demo_exponential_vs_linear()
    demo_depth()
    demo_bit_split()
    demo_end_to_end()
    print("=" * 78)
    print("SUMMARY:  values are 1-Lipschitz and free; keys admit no Lipschitz")
    print("constant, no codebook of fixed cardinality rescues them, their damage")
    print("is exponential and compounds with depth.  Deploy K>=8 bits / V=4 bits.")
    print("=" * 78)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
",
    "demo_measurement_reconciliation": """"Reconciling the measured arms with the theory, and pricing a cache budget.

This short script does three things with the reported perplexity measurements
(full-precision control 7.1093, context length 2048, held-out text slice):

  1. recomputes every reported percentage change and the key-versus-value damage
     ratio directly from the raw perplexities, so no headline number is quoted
     rather than derived;
  2. checks the qualitative predictions of the theory against the arms: value
     quantisation must be near-free (1-Lipschitz read-out), key quantisation may
     be arbitrarily bad, and no richer 4-bit key format may rescue the keys;
  3. prices candidate cache configurations under the first-order damage model
     D(b_K, b_V) = A/2^{b_K} + 1/2^{b_V} and prints the recommended allocation
     together with its memory saving relative to a 16-bit cache.

Pure standard library; run with `python3 demo2.py`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

CONTROL_PPL: float = 7.1093

ARMS: List[Tuple[str, float]] = [
    ("K q4_1 / V q4_1  (4-bit scale+offset, both halves)", 3158.07),
    ("K iq4_nl / V iq4_nl (4-bit nonuniform, both halves)", 1627.35),
    ("K q4_0 / V f16   (4-bit KEYS only)", 2537.80),
    ("K f16 / V q4_0   (4-bit VALUES only)", 7.1211),
]


def percent_change(ppl: float, control: float = CONTROL_PPL) -> float:
    """Relative perplexity change in percent."""
    return 100.0 * (ppl - control) / control


def damage(A: Fraction, b_key: int, b_val: int) -> Fraction:
    """First-order damage model: the key term carries the amplification A."""
    return A / Fraction(2) ** b_key + Fraction(1) / Fraction(2) ** b_val


def average_bits(b_key: int, b_val: int) -> float:
    """Mean bits per cache element for a (b_key, b_val) split."""
    return (b_key + b_val) / 2.0


def report_arms() -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Print the measured arms with derived percentages; return the key stats."""
    print("Measured arms (control perplexity %.4f)" % CONTROL_PPL)
    print(f"  {'arm':<54}{'PPL':>11}{'dPPL':>13}")
    stats: Dict[str, float] = {}
    for name, ppl in ARMS:
        pc = percent_change(ppl)
        stats[name] = pc
        print(f"  {name:<54}{ppl:11.4f}{pc:12.3f}%")
    keys_only = percent_change(2537.80)
    values_only = percent_change(7.1211)
    ratio = keys_only / values_only
    print(f"\n  keys-only damage / values-only damage = {ratio:,.0f} : 1")
    print(f"  (keys cost {keys_only:,.0f}% ; values cost {values_only:.3f}%)")
    return {"keys_only": keys_only, "values_only": values_only, "ratio": ratio}


def check_predictions() -> None:
    """Confront the three qualitative predictions with the arms."""
    print("\nPredictions versus measurement")
    v = percent_change(7.1211)
    k = percent_change(2537.80)
    q41 = percent_change(3158.07)
    q40 = percent_change(2537.80)
    checks = [
        ("values are essentially free (1-Lipschitz read-out)", v < 1.0),
        ("keys are catastrophic at 4 bits", k > 1000.0),
        ("asymmetry exceeds the predicted 5x by orders of magnitude",
         k / v > 1000.0),
        ("a richer 4-bit key format does NOT rescue the keys "
         "(scale+offset no better than the plain grid)", q41 >= q40),
    ]
    for text, ok in checks:
        print(f"  [{'OK ' if ok else 'NO '}] {text}")


def price_budgets(A: Fraction = Fraction(16)) -> None:
    """Price candidate cache configurations and recommend an allocation."""
    print(f"\nPricing cache configurations at amplification A = {A}")
    print(f"  {'config':<12}{'avg bits':>10}{'damage':>14}{'memory vs f16':>16}")
    configs = [(16, 16), (8, 16), (16, 4), (8, 8), (6, 6), (8, 4), (4, 8), (4, 4)]
    rows = []
    for bk, bv in configs:
        d = damage(A, bk, bv)
        avg = average_bits(bk, bv)
        rows.append((bk, bv, avg, d))
        print(f"  K{bk:<2}/V{bv:<7}{avg:10.1f}{float(d):14.6f}"
              f"{avg / 16.0:15.1%}")
    feasible = [r for r in rows if r[2] <= 6.0]
    best = min(feasible, key=lambda r: r[3])
    print(f"\n  best configuration at <= 6 average bits: "
          f"K{best[0]}/V{best[1]} (damage {float(best[3]):.6f}, "
          f"{best[2] / 16.0:.0%} of a 16-bit cache)")
    print("  the equal split K6/V6 at the same average bit rate is "
          f"{float(damage(A, 6, 6) / damage(A, 8, 4)):.2f}x worse")


def main() -> None:
    report_arms()
    check_predictions()
    price_budgets()
    print("\nConclusion: split the budget by role — keys >= 8 bits, values may take 4.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
",
    "algorithm_bit_allocation": """"Role-split bit allocation: exact minimisation of the first-order damage model.

D_A(b_K, b_V) = A / 2^{b_K} + 1 / 2^{b_V},  subject to b_K + b_V = T.

The key term carries the amplification factor A (the query norm times the key
range); the value term does not.  Because D_A(b, T - b) = A*2^{-b} + 2^{b-T} is
a sum of two exponentials with opposite slopes, it is strictly convex in b, so
the integer optimum is one of the two integers adjacent to the real minimiser
(T + log2 A)/2.  We compute both the closed form and an exhaustive exact check
in rational arithmetic, so the answer carries no floating-point doubt.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Tuple


def damage(A: Fraction, b_key: int, b_val: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact first-order damage of a (b_key, b_val)-bit cache."""
    return A / Fraction(2) ** b_key + Fraction(1) / Fraction(2) ** b_val


def shift_bit_helps(A: Fraction, b_key: int, b_val: int) -> bool:
    """True iff moving one bit from the values to the keys strictly reduces damage.

    The criterion is 2^{b_K} < A * 2^{b_V}: the equilibrium is the point where
    the amplified key term balances the value term.
    """
    return Fraction(2) ** b_key < A * Fraction(2) ** b_val


def optimal_split_closed_form(A: float, total_bits: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """Closed-form optimum: b_K = round((T + log2 A) / 2), clipped to [0, T]."""
    b = round((total_bits + math.log2(A)) / 2.0)
    b = max(0, min(total_bits, int(b)))
    return b, total_bits - b


def optimal_split_exact(A: Fraction, total_bits: int) -> Tuple[int, int, Fraction]:
    """Exhaustive exact minimisation over all integer splits.  O(T) work."""
    candidates: List[Tuple[int, int, Fraction]] = [
        (b, total_bits - b, damage(A, b, total_bits - b))
        for b in range(total_bits + 1)
    ]
    return min(candidates, key=lambda t: t[2])


def allocate(A: Fraction, total_bits: int) -> dict:
    """Full allocation report: optimum, its damage, and the uniform baseline."""
    b_key, b_val, d_opt = optimal_split_exact(A, total_bits)
    b_half = total_bits // 2
    d_uniform = damage(A, b_half, total_bits - b_half)
    return {
        "amplification": A,
        "total_bits": total_bits,
        "optimal_key_bits": b_key,
        "optimal_value_bits": b_val,
        "optimal_damage": d_opt,
        "uniform_damage": d_uniform,
        "improvement_factor": d_uniform / d_opt,
        "closed_form_agrees": optimal_split_closed_form(float(A), total_bits)
        == (b_key, b_val),
    }


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for A, T in ((Fraction(16), 12), (Fraction(16), 16), (Fraction(64), 12),
                 (Fraction(256), 20)):
        r = allocate(A, T)
        print(f"A = {str(A):>4}, budget {T:>2} bits ->  "
              f"K{r['optimal_key_bits']}/V{r['optimal_value_bits']}  "
              f"damage {str(r['optimal_damage']):>12}  "
              f"({float(r['improvement_factor']):.2f}x better than uniform, "
              f"closed form agrees: {r['closed_form_agrees']})")
",
    "algorithm_key_bitwidth": """"Certified safe key bit-width from a margin distribution.

A b-bit key grid covering the key range [-R, R] moves each stored entry by at
most res(R, b) = R / 2^b, hence moves each attention logit by at most
||q||_1 * res(R, b).  A top-1 decision whose logit margin exceeds twice that
quantity therefore survives quantisation intact.  Consequently

    b bits are safe for all decisions of margin >= m   <=>   2^b > 2||q||_1 R / m,

i.e. b = floor(log2(2||q||_1 R / m)) + 1.  The requirement is *logarithmic* in
the amplification ||q||_1 R / m: each extra key bit doubles the query norm (or
halves the margin) that can be tolerated, which is why the degradation is a
threshold in bits rather than a smooth slope.

Given an empirical margin sample we can go further and report, for each
bit-width, the fraction of decisions that are certified to survive — a directly
actionable curve for choosing a cache format.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Dict, List, Sequence


def res(key_range: float, bits: int) -> float:
    """Worst-case per-entry rounding error of a uniform `bits`-bit grid."""
    return key_range / 2.0 ** bits


def logit_error_bound(l1_query_norm: float, key_range: float, bits: int) -> float:
    """Guaranteed logit perturbation ||q||_1 * res(R, b)."""
    return l1_query_norm * res(key_range, bits)


def safe_bits_for_margin(l1_query_norm: float, key_range: float,
                         margin: float) -> int:
    """Least b with 2 * ||q||_1 * res(R, b) < margin."""
    if margin <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("margin must be positive")
    need = 2.0 * l1_query_norm * key_range / margin
    return max(0, math.floor(math.log2(need)) + 1)


def certified_fraction(margins: Sequence[float], l1_query_norm: float,
                       key_range: float, bits: int) -> float:
    """Fraction of observed decisions certified to survive a b-bit key cache."""
    threshold = 2.0 * logit_error_bound(l1_query_norm, key_range, bits)
    return sum(1 for m in margins if m > threshold) / len(margins)


def bitwidth_report(margins: Sequence[float], l1_query_norm: float,
                    key_range: float, bit_grid: Sequence[int] = (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16),
                    target_coverage: float = 0.999) -> Dict[str, object]:
    """Full report: coverage per bit-width and the least width meeting the target."""
    coverage: List[Dict[str, float]] = [
        {"bits": b,
         "logit_error": logit_error_bound(l1_query_norm, key_range, b),
         "certified_fraction": certified_fraction(margins, l1_query_norm,
                                                  key_range, b)}
        for b in bit_grid
    ]
    recommended = next((c["bits"] for c in coverage
                        if c["certified_fraction"] >= target_coverage), None)
    return {"coverage": coverage,
            "target_coverage": target_coverage,
            "recommended_key_bits": recommended}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import random

    rng = random.Random(0)
    # A plausible margin distribution: mostly decisive tokens, a heavy tail of
    # near-ties (the tokens that a coarse key cache destroys first).
    margins = [abs(rng.gauss(2.0, 1.2)) for _ in range(20000)]
    l1q, R = 64.0, 1.0

    print(f"||q||_1 = {l1q}, key range R = {R}, {len(margins)} sampled margins")
    print(f"{'bits':>6} {'logit error':>14} {'certified':>12}")
    rep = bitwidth_report(margins, l1q, R)
    for row in rep["coverage"]:
        print(f"{row['bits']:6d} {row['logit_error']:14.6f} "
              f"{row['certified_fraction']:12.4%}")
    print(f"recommended key bit-width at "
          f"{rep['target_coverage']:.1%} coverage: {rep['recommended_key_bits']}")
    print(f"worst-case criterion for margin 1.0: "
          f"{safe_bits_for_margin(l1q, R, 1.0)} bits")
",
    "algorithm_collision_audit": """"Pigeonhole codebook-collision audit for candidate key quantisers.

A key quantiser is any map Q from reals to a finite codebook C, with no
structural assumption whatsoever: uniform grids, scale-and-offset block formats,
nonuniform fitted codebooks, learned lattices.  If |C| <= N then evaluating Q on
the N+1 equally spaced probes 0, 1/N, ..., 1 must produce a repeat, by the
pigeonhole principle.  Any repeated pair a != b is a pair of *distinguishable*
keys that the format stores identically, separated by at least 1/N.

The audit then constructs the adversarial query q = 2/(a - b), whose magnitude
is at most 2N.  With that query, the exact two-position cache (a, b) has a logit
gap of exactly 2, so its attention read-out exceeds 3/4, while the stored cache
(Q(a), Q(a)) is a perfect tie with read-out exactly 1/2.  The certified damage
is therefore at least 1/4, independently of the internal design of Q.

Complexity: N+1 quantiser evaluations and O(N) hashing; O(N) memory.  The audit
never fails to find a witness for a format of cardinality at most N, so it turns
"is this new 4-bit key format safe?" into a terminating computation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Callable, Dict, Optional, Tuple


def softmax_two(a: float, b: float) -> float:
    """Weight the softmax places on position 0 given logits (a, b)."""
    m = max(a, b)
    ea, eb = math.exp(a - m), math.exp(b - m)
    return ea / (ea + eb)


def audit_key_quantiser(Q: Callable[[float], float], n_probes: int,
                        lo: float = 0.0, hi: float = 1.0) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
    """Search for a collision witness; return a full damage certificate.

    Returns None only if Q separated all n_probes+1 probes, which proves its
    codebook has more than n_probes entries on this interval.
    """
    seen: Dict[float, float] = {}
    span = hi - lo
    for i in range(n_probes + 1):
        x = lo + span * i / n_probes
        code = Q(x)
        if code in seen:
            a, b = seen[code], x
            query = 2.0 / (a - b)
            exact = softmax_two(query * a, query * b)
            stored = softmax_two(query * code, query * code)
            return {
                "key_a": a,
                "key_b": b,
                "separation": abs(a - b),
                "separation_bound": span / n_probes,
                "shared_code": code,
                "adversarial_query": query,
                "query_magnitude_bound": 2.0 * n_probes / span,
                "exact_readout": exact,
                "stored_readout": stored,
                "certified_damage": abs(exact - stored),
            }
        seen[code] = x
    return None


def audit_bitwidth(Q: Callable[[float], float], bits: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
    """Audit a format advertised as `bits`-bit, i.e. of cardinality 2^bits."""
    return audit_key_quantiser(Q, n_probes=2 ** bits)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    NONUNIFORM = [0.0, 0.004, 0.012, 0.027, 0.051, 0.086, 0.135, 0.203,
                  0.292, 0.404, 0.539, 0.667, 0.775, 0.867, 0.941, 1.0]

    formats: Dict[str, Callable[[float], float]] = {
        "uniform 4-bit grid": lambda x: round(x * 15.0) / 15.0,
        "scale+offset 4-bit": lambda x: round((x - 0.0) / (1.0 / 15.0)) * (1.0 / 15.0),
        "nonuniform 4-bit codebook": lambda x: min(NONUNIFORM, key=lambda c: abs(c - x)),
        "uniform 8-bit grid": lambda x: round(x * 255.0) / 255.0,
    }

    for name, Q in formats.items():
        bits = 8 if "8-bit" in name else 4
        cert = audit_bitwidth(Q, bits)
        print(f"{name}:")
        if cert is None:
            print("    no collision found at this probe budget")
            continue
        print(f"    collides {cert['key_a']:.6f} and {cert['key_b']:.6f}"
              f"  (separation {cert['separation']:.6f}"
              f" >= {cert['separation_bound']:.6f})")
        print(f"    adversarial query {cert['adversarial_query']:.3f}"
              f"  (|q| <= {cert['query_magnitude_bound']:.1f})")
        print(f"    read-out {cert['exact_readout']:.6f} -> "
              f"{cert['stored_readout']:.6f}"
              f"   certified damage {cert['certified_damage']:.6f}")
",
    "visualization_cliff_curves": """"Visualisation: the cliff — exponential key damage versus linear value damage.

Plots the two terms of the guaranteed read-out budget

    (exp(2 * ||q||_1 * delta_K) - 1) * B     [keys]        and     delta_V   [values]

against bit-width, on a logarithmic damage axis, for several query norms.  The
value curve is a straight line of slope -1 per bit (halving); the key curves
plunge only once the exponent has come down, producing the characteristic knee —
the cliff — a couple of bits wide.  A horizontal line at damage 1 marks the
scale at which a single attention read-out is entirely rewritten.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def key_term(bits: int, l1_query: float, key_range: float = 1.0,
             value_bound: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """(exp(2 ||q||_1 R / 2^b) - 1) * B, clipped for plotting."""
    exponent = 2.0 * l1_query * key_range / 2.0 ** bits
    return (math.expm1(min(exponent, 60.0))) * value_bound


def value_term(bits: int, value_range: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """delta_V = R_V / 2^b."""
    return value_range / 2.0 ** bits


def main() -> None:
    bit_grid: List[int] = list(range(1, 17))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.0, 5.6))

    for l1q, colour in ((16.0, "#e4572e"), (64.0, "#c0392b"), (256.0, "#7d1128")):
        ax.plot(bit_grid, [key_term(b, l1q) for b in bit_grid],
                marker="o", ms=4, color=colour, lw=2,
                label=fr"key damage, $\|q\|_1 = {int(l1q)}$")

    ax.plot(bit_grid, [value_term(b) for b in bit_grid],
            marker="s", ms=4, color="#1b6ca8", lw=2.5,
            label="value damage (any query, any depth)")

    ax.axhline(1.0, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1.0)
    ax.text(15.6, 1.15, "output fully rewritten", ha="right", fontsize=9,
            color="#555555")
    ax.axvspan(3.5, 4.5, color="#c0392b", alpha=0.08)
    ax.text(4.0, 1e-6, "4 bits", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#c0392b")
    ax.axvspan(7.5, 8.5, color="#1b6ca8", alpha=0.08)
    ax.text(8.0, 1e-6, "8 bits", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#1b6ca8")

    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel("bits per cache element")
    ax.set_ylabel("guaranteed read-out damage (log scale)")
    ax.set_title("Keys own the cliff: exponential key term, linear value term")
    ax.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper right")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("cliff_curves.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote cliff_curves.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
",
    "visualization_bit_budget": """"Visualisation: the bit-budget landscape and the location of the optimum.

Left panel: the exact damage D_A(b, T - b) = A/2^b + 1/2^{T-b} as a function of
the key bit-width b, at a fixed total budget T, for several amplification
factors A.  Each curve is a strictly convex "V" in log space whose minimum sits
where the amplified key term balances the value term, i.e. at 2^b = A 2^{T-b};
the optimum is marked.  At A = 16 and T = 12 the minimum is exactly K8/V4.

Right panel: how the optimal key bit-width moves with the amplification.  The
optimum grows like (T + log2 A)/2 — every quadrupling of the key amplification
buys the keys one more bit at the values' expense.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def damage(A: Fraction, b_key: int, b_val: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact first-order damage model."""
    return A / Fraction(2) ** b_key + Fraction(1) / Fraction(2) ** b_val


def optimum(A: Fraction, total: int) -> Tuple[int, Fraction]:
    """Exhaustive exact minimiser over integer splits of `total` bits."""
    best_b = min(range(total + 1), key=lambda b: damage(A, b, total - b))
    return best_b, damage(A, best_b, total - best_b)


def main() -> None:
    total = 12
    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12.5, 5.2))

    for A, colour in ((Fraction(4), "#5b8c5a"), (Fraction(16), "#c0392b"),
                      (Fraction(64), "#7d1128")):
        bs: List[int] = list(range(total + 1))
        ds = [float(damage(A, b, total - b)) for b in bs]
        ax1.plot(bs, ds, marker="o", ms=4, lw=2, color=colour,
                 label=fr"$A = {int(A)}$")
        b_opt, d_opt = optimum(A, total)
        ax1.scatter([b_opt], [float(d_opt)], s=110, facecolors="none",
                    edgecolors=colour, lw=2.0, zorder=5)
        ax1.annotate(f"K{b_opt}/V{total - b_opt}", (b_opt, float(d_opt)),
                     textcoords="offset points", xytext=(6, -14),
                     color=colour, fontsize=10)

    ax1.axvline(total / 2, color="#888888", ls=":", lw=1.2)
    ax1.text(total / 2 + 0.15, 8.0, "uniform split", rotation=90,
             fontsize=9, color="#888888", va="top")
    ax1.set_yscale("log")
    ax1.set_xlabel("key bits $b_K$  (value bits are $12 - b_K$)")
    ax1.set_ylabel("guaranteed damage $D_A(b_K, 12-b_K)$")
    ax1.set_title("A 12-bit budget: where should the bits go?")
    ax1.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
    ax1.legend(frameon=False)

    amps = [2 ** e for e in range(0, 13)]
    opts = [optimum(Fraction(A), total)[0] for A in amps]
    ax2.step([math.log2(A) for A in amps], opts, where="mid", lw=2.2,
             color="#1b6ca8", marker="o", ms=5)
    ax2.plot([math.log2(A) for A in amps],
             [(total + math.log2(A)) / 2 for A in amps],
             ls="--", lw=1.4, color="#c0392b",
             label=r"continuous optimum $(T + \log_2 A)/2$")
    ax2.set_xlabel(r"$\log_2 A$   (key amplification)")
    ax2.set_ylabel("optimal key bits")
    ax2.set_title("The optimum drifts toward the keys as amplification grows")
    ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.25)
    ax2.legend(frameon=False, loc="upper left")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("bit_budget_landscape.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote bit_budget_landscape.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
",
    "visualization_depth": """"Visualisation: depth turns a per-head asymmetry into a model-level collapse.

The key perturbation obeys an amplifying recursion e_{l+1} >= gamma * e_l with
gamma > 1, so e_L >= gamma^L e_0 and the error passes every threshold at some
finite depth.  The value perturbation obeys an averaging recursion
e_{l+1} <= max(eps, e_l), so it never leaves its initial band, at any depth.

The figure traces both, for several amplification factors gamma, against layer
index, and marks the depth at which each key trace first reaches the "decision
destroyed" level of 1/4 — the level at which a two-way attention choice flips
from decisive to a coin toss.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def key_trace(e0: float, gamma: float, depth: int) -> List[float]:
    """Amplifying recursion: e_{l+1} = gamma * e_l."""
    out, e = [e0], e0
    for _ in range(depth):
        e *= gamma
        out.append(e)
    return out


def value_trace(e0: float, eps: float, depth: int) -> List[float]:
    """Averaging recursion: e_{l+1} <= max(eps, e_l), started inside the band."""
    return [min(e0, eps)] * (depth + 1)


def main() -> None:
    depth, e0, eps = 32, 1e-4, 1e-4
    layers = list(range(depth + 1))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.2, 5.6))

    for gamma, colour in ((1.15, "#e4956b"), (1.35, "#c0392b"), (1.6, "#7d1128")):
        trace = key_trace(e0, gamma, depth)
        ax.plot(layers, trace, lw=2.2, color=colour,
                label=fr"key error, $\gamma = {gamma}$")
        hit = next((L for L, e in enumerate(trace) if e >= 0.25), None)
        if hit is not None:
            ax.scatter([hit], [trace[hit]], s=90, color=colour, zorder=5)
            ax.annotate(f"layer {hit}", (hit, trace[hit]),
                        textcoords="offset points", xytext=(-42, 6),
                        color=colour, fontsize=9)

    ax.plot(layers, value_trace(e0, eps, depth), lw=2.6, color="#1b6ca8",
            label=r"value error (band $\varepsilon$, all depths)")
    ax.axhline(0.25, color="#555555", ls="--", lw=1.1)
    ax.text(0.4, 0.30, "decision destroyed", fontsize=9, color="#555555")

    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xlabel("layer index $\\ell$")
    ax.set_ylabel("perturbation magnitude (log scale)")
    ax.set_title("Multiplication runs away; averaging does not")
    ax.grid(True, which="both", alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, loc="lower right")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("depth_amplification.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote depth_amplification.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

concept.title: FACT round-74 #6 — ECM-STAGE2-WALL: the recorded destruction wall does not exist under outcome-separated accounting — B1 ≥ p+1+2√p makes every curve succeed, not die (self-audit of paper 159)
concept.concept_description:
**Paper 215 · exp 568 · round-74 #6 · assessment v322**

VERDICT: **H3 CONFIRMED (strong form)** — H1/H0 moot-by-absence.

Paper 159 headlines an ECM self-destruction wall: "when B1 ≳ min(p,q), every Hasse-window order divides lcm(1..B1), all curves degenerate simultaneously, uncapped E[T] infinite", with a validity edge B1 ≲ min(p,q)/2. Exp568 tests that boundary under outcome-separated accounting {found_p, found_q, dead, nothing}.

**Design.** Bitlen-26 q≫p stratum (generator nextprime(3p+U[1,200))), n_N=40/cell, grid B1/p ∈ {0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 0.9, 1.05} × arms B2/B1 ∈ {1 (control), 4, 16}; guarded affine EC ops reused VERBATIM from exp488_true_ecm.py (validated there 10/10 ladder + 100/100 mod-12); true-lcm stage-1 schedule; NEW true difference-stage stage-2. Pre-registration verbatim before any data: H1 slope(log w* vs log(B2/B1)) CI covers 1 / H0 covers 0 / MIXED; H3 ADDED after reading the mechanism sentence, BEFORE data (timing disclosed): the wall is a detection/accounting artifact — gcd(den,N)==N 'dead' events or missing p-vs-q separation — not method failure.

**Results (600 trials).**
- ZERO 'dead' outcomes in the entire grid.
- Success 1.000 in every cell at B1/p ≥ 0.25; **6/6 cells at 1.000 at B1/p = 0.9 AND 1.05** — exactly where paper 159 records uncapped E[T] infinite.
- Only misses: two low-edge cells at B1/p = 0.125 (arm-4 0.875, arm-16 0.95), all misses 'nothing', never 'dead'.
- No w* exists anywhere → H1/H0 never arm.

**Mechanism (pre-data note, vindicated).** B1 ≥ p+1+2√p ⇒ every Hasse-window order n ≤ B1 ⇒ every prime power l^e ‖ n has l^e ≤ B1 ⇒ n | lcm(1..B1) ⇒ [L]P = O mod p on EVERY curve ⇒ first guarded inversion with vanishing denominator returns gcd = p: GUARANTEED SUCCESS, not death. Simultaneous degeneracy mod q impossible for q ≫ B1. "All curves degenerate" can only have read as death if accounting conflated gcd=p wins with gcd=N losses or lacked p-vs-q separation.

**Structural insight (ledger-grade).** Guarded-affine accounting carries a scale-independent random-collision baseline ≈ 1 − exp(−c·B1/p) (#ops ~ 1.44·B1, per-op hit ~1/p): ~17% predicted at B1/p = 0.125 vs 68% observed found-p share (collision-luck + order-divisibility mixed). # Exact two-prime outcome counts, and how a non-injective ledger manufactures a wall

The audit of paper 159 turns on an accounting question: which recorded outcome does a
guarded inversion with `gcd = p` get filed under?  This file makes both halves of that
question exact.

**Exact counts.**  In the standard cyclic model — a random point is a uniformly random
pair of residues `(a, b) ∈ ℤ/m_p × ℤ/m_q`, one coordinate per prime factor of
`N = p·q` — the four separated outcomes partition `m_p · m_q` trials into blocks whose
sizes are products of the two firing counts:

* `card_deadSet`      : `gcd(m_p,k) · gcd(m_q,k)`
* `card_foundPSet`    : `gcd(m_p,k) · (m_q − gcd(m_q,k))`
* `card_foundQSet`    : `(m_p − gcd(m_p,k)) · gcd(m_q,k)`
* `card_nothingSet`   : `(m_p − gcd(m_p,k)) · (m_q − gcd(m_q,k))`
* `card_add_card_eq`  : the four blocks sum to `m_p · m_q`.

**The wall, exactly.**  `reveal_eq_empty_of_both_cover` shows that when the bound covers
*both* group orders every trial is `dead` and the reveal count is `0`: a genuine wall
exists, and it sits at `max(p,q)`.  `reveal_monotone_of_inert_q` shows that as long as
the mod-`q` side stays inert the reveal count is monotone in `B`, so nothing wall-shaped
can happen at `min(p,q)`.  `reveal_drops_two_two` is an explicit two-line witness of the
real wall.

**Ledger faithfulness.**  A ledger is a map from the firing pattern `(fires mod p,
fires mod q)` to a recorded outcome.  `canonicalLedger_faithful` states that the
separated ledger is injective; `wallLedger_not_faithful` and
`wallLedger_manufactures_wall` show that the single conflation "file a `p`-side firing
as a death" is non-injective and reproduces, verbatim, the recorded wall sentence on
inputs where the truth is `found_p`.

namespace ECMWall

open ECMStage1 Finset

/-! ## The complement of the firing set -/

/-- Residues that are *not* killed by the scalar. -/
def coFiringSet (m k : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := Finset.range m \ firingSet m k

theorem firingSet_subset_range (m k : ℕ) : firingSet m k ⊆ Finset.range m :=
  Finset.filter_subset _ _

theorem card_coFiringSet {m k : ℕ} (hm : 0 < m) :
    (coFiringSet m k).card = m - Nat.gcd m k := by
  rw [coFiringSet, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset (firingSet_subset_range m k),
    Finset.card_range, card_firingSet _ _ hm]

/-! ## The four separated outcome blocks -/

variable (mp mq k : ℕ)

/-- Trials revealing `p`: the mod-`p` coordinate fires, the mod-`q` one does not. -/
def foundPSet : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := firingSet mp k ×ˢ coFiringSet mq k

/-- Trials revealing `q`. -/
def foundQSet : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := coFiringSet mp k ×ˢ firingSet mq k

/-- Trials in which both coordinates degenerate: the guarded inversion returns `N`. -/
def deadSet : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := firingSet mp k ×ˢ firingSet mq k

/-- Trials in which nothing degenerates. -/
def nothingSet : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := coFiringSet mp k ×ˢ coFiringSet mq k

/-- Trials revealing a proper factor of `N`. -/
def revealSet : Finset (ℕ × ℕ) := foundPSet mp mq k ∪ foundQSet mp mq k

variable {mp mq k}

theorem card_deadSet (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (deadSet mp mq k).card = Nat.gcd mp k * Nat.gcd mq k := by
  rw [deadSet, Finset.card_product, card_firingSet _ _ hp, card_firingSet _ _ hq]

theorem card_foundPSet (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (foundPSet mp mq k).card = Nat.gcd mp k * (mq - Nat.gcd mq k) := by
  rw [foundPSet, Finset.card_product, card_firingSet _ _ hp, card_coFiringSet hq]

theorem card_foundQSet (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (foundQSet mp mq k).card = (mp - Nat.gcd mp k) * Nat.gcd mq k := by
  rw [foundQSet, Finset.card_product, card_coFiringSet hp, card_firingSet _ _ hq]

theorem card_nothingSet (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (nothingSet mp mq k).card = (mp - Nat.gcd mp k) * (mq - Nat.gcd mq k) := by
  rw [nothingSet, Finset.card_product, card_coFiringSet hp, card_coFiringSet hq]

/-- The four blocks account for every trial. -/
theorem card_add_card_eq (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (deadSet mp mq k).card + (foundPSet mp mq k).card + (foundQSet mp mq k).card
      + (nothingSet mp mq k).card = mp * mq := by
  have h1 : Nat.gcd mp k ≤ mp := Nat.le_of_dvd hp (Nat.gcd_dvd_left _ _)
  have h2 : Nat.gcd mq k ≤ mq := Nat.le_of_dvd hq (Nat.gcd_dvd_left _ _)
  rw [card_deadSet hp hq, card_foundPSet hp hq, card_foundQSet hp hq,
    card_nothingSet hp hq]
  zify [h1, h2]
  ring

    Disjoint (foundPSet mp mq k) (foundQSet mp mq k) := by
  refine Finset.disjoint_left.mpr ?_
  rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ha hb
  simp only [foundPSet, foundQSet, coFiringSet, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_sdiff] at ha hb
  exact hb.1.2 ha.1

theorem card_revealSet (hp : 0 < mp) (hq : 0 < mq) :
    (revealSet mp mq k).card =
      Nat.gcd mp k * (mq - Nat.gcd mq k) + (mp - Nat.gcd mp k) * Nat.gcd mq k := by
  rw [revealSet, Finset.card_union_of_disjoint foundPSet_disjoint_foundQSet,
    card_foundPSet hp hq, card_foundQSet hp hq]
